hook: Engineers just finished carving a 14km tunnel link directly under London.

sections.voiceover: Engineers just finished carving a 14km tunnel link directly under London.
sections.visual_cue: Top-down view of the tunnel route map connecting to the station site.

sections.voiceover: How deep is the station box, the massive concrete structure housing the new underground platforms?
sections.visual_cue: Animated cross-section showing the tunnel boring machine breaking through into the station box.

sections.voiceover: The station box at Old Oak Common reaches a massive 20 metres of underground depth.
sections.visual_cue: Wide shot of the deep, concrete-lined station box construction site.

sections.voiceover: They built twin 360m mined tunnels as part of the 14km HS2 high-speed rail link. This breakthrough completes the 14km tunnel link for the Skanska Costain Strabag project.
sections.visual_cue: Detailed diagram highlighting the twin mined tunnel segments connecting to the station infrastructure.

sections.voiceover: Old Oak Common serves as the primary station for this 14km HS2 high-speed rail link.
sections.visual_cue: Aerial view of the completed station box structure integrated into the landscape.
